hints: Split the modulus equation into the two sign cases for $5^x-1$.
Solve $4(5^x-1)=\pm5^x$ to obtain two positive values of $5^x$.
Take logarithms base $5$ for each and round only the final $x$-values.
walkthrough: Split the modulus equation $4|5^x - 1| = 5^x$ into two linear cases in $5^x$:

Solve Case 1 for $x$ by taking natural logarithms:
$$x\ln 5 = \ln\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$$
$$x = \dfrac{\ln(4/3)}{\ln 5} \approx \dfrac{0.287682}{1.609438} \approx 0.178747 \dots \approx 0.179$$

Solve Case 2 for $x$ by taking natural logarithms:
$$x\ln 5 = \ln(0.8)$$
$$x = \dfrac{\ln(0.8)}{\ln 5} \approx \dfrac{-0.223144}{1.609438} \approx -0.138647 \dots \approx -0.139$$

State both solutions correct to 3 decimal places:
$$x = 0.179, \quad -0.139$$
